events.title: Founders start Hotspot, their first startup
events.summary: Before Tally, the founders worked on Hotspot, a platform connecting hotels with travel influencers, started in June 2019.

events.title: Founders pivot from Hotspot to build Tally
events.summary: Hotspot lost half its clients by July 2020 due to COVID-19. In August 2020 the founders decided to pivot to building Tally.

events.title: MVP shared with friends and family
events.summary: Tally first shared its MVP with friends and family in August 2020.

events.title: Tally beta/MVP released
events.summary: Tally released its beta version in September 2020 and worked with early users to shape the product. Other claims place the launch in summer or October 2020.

events.title: Cold outreach to early users on Product Hunt and Twitter
events.summary: The founders did cold outreach to hundreds of prospects found on Product Hunt and Twitter. They also sought feedback in Slack communities and invited early users to a Slack channel.

events.title: First integration: Google Sheets
events.summary: Tally's first integration, with Google Sheets, shipped on September 18, 2020.

events.title: Paid Tally Pro plan introduced
events.summary: Tally introduced its paid Tally Pro plan on October 10, 2020. A single tier was later described as $29/month or $290/year.

events.title: Zapier integration launched in beta
events.summary: Tally launched a Zapier integration in beta on November 9, 2020.

events.title: Planned Product Hunt launch postponed
events.summary: Tally postponed its planned December 2020 Product Hunt launch because the founders' daughter was born early.

events.title: Product Hunt launch
events.summary: Tally launched on Product Hunt in March 2021. It led for about 23 hours but missed #1 product of the day. The company says the launch doubled its users from about 1,500 to 3,000.

events.title: Notion integration made available to all users
events.summary: After a private beta in April 2021, the Notion integration became available to all users in May 2021 when Notion's API went public.

events.title: Startup program, discounts and affiliate program
events.summary: Around June 2021 Tally launched a startup program, discounts for students and non-profits, and an affiliate program. The affiliate program pays 20% recurring commission.

events.title: Product-market fit survey
events.summary: In August 2021 Tally measured product-market fit using Superhuman's survey process.

events.title: Founders on Indie Hackers podcast
events.summary: Tally's founders were invited to the Indie Hackers podcast in September 2021.

events.title: First meetup in Barcelona
events.summary: Tally organized its first meetup in Barcelona on April 26, 2023 as part of No-Code Week. It featured demos from Notion, Make and Framer.

events.title: First hire: customer success manager
events.summary: Tally's first hire was a customer success manager, made to scale support beyond the two founders.

events.title: Tally 2.0 launch on Product Hunt
events.summary: Tally 2.0 launched on Product Hunt on September 19, 2023 with a new logo, redesigned dashboard, command menu and 2FA. It became #1 Product of the Day, Week and Month.

events.title: Golden Kitty win in Bootstrapped category
events.summary: Tally won a Golden Kitty as best bootstrapped product following the Tally 2.0 launch.

events.title: Featured in The Verge's Installer newsletter
events.summary: As a result of the Tally 2.0 launch, Tally was featured in The Verge's Installer newsletter. The feature brought 1.7K unique visitors.

events.title: Tally Business tier launched
events.summary: Tally launched a Tally Business tier for larger organizations and said it had no plans to raise Tally Pro's price.

events.title: First office at Ghent's Wintercircus
events.summary: Tally moved into its first office at the Wintercircus in Ghent.

events.title: Experiments with YouTube influencer partnerships
events.summary: In 2024 Tally began experimenting with paid marketing via YouTube influencer partnerships, with 10 videos live at the time.

events.title: Shift to Pro features and conversion; first search ads
events.summary: After two years without new Pro features, Tally shifted focus to conversion with highly requested Pro features. It also launched its first-ever search ads as an experiment. Tally says the premium features led to an uptick in Pro upgrades.

events.title: Public API enters public beta
events.summary: Tally's public API entered public beta, free for everyone, on June 4, 2025.

events.title: MCP server released in beta
events.summary: Tally released an MCP server in beta on July 11, 2025 for creating forms through AI assistants like Claude.

events.title: ChatGPT becomes #1 referral source
events.summary: In 2025 ChatGPT became Tally's #1 referral source. Tally attributes this to years of authentic presence in forums, Reddit and UGC.

events.title: Revenue targets dropped for 2026
events.summary: In January 2026 Tally dropped revenue targets to focus on product quality, tracking NPS and feedback instead. It also ruled out enterprise plans, sales calls and big launches for 2026.

events.title: First Tally-organized meetup in London
events.summary: Tally hosted its first Tally-organized meetup in London in June 2026.

events.title: Tally AI for everyone and Typeform import
events.summary: On July 8, 2026 Tally made Tally AI available to everyone and launched one-click Typeform import.

events.title: ChatGPT plugin, Claude and Superhuman Go connectors
events.summary: Tally launched an official ChatGPT plugin, a verified Claude connector and a Superhuman Go connector on August 27, 2026.

events.title: A marketing team member hired as marketing manager

company_stages.label: Two-founder bootstrapped, customer-funded business
company_stages.summary: Tally Pro was introduced in October 2020. The founders say Tally has been cash-flow positive from the start. For about two years the co-founders ran it alone as a profitable, bootstrapped business funded by subscriptions. MRR rose from $64 in October 2020 to $30K in October 2022.

company_stages.label: Small bootstrapped team past $100K MRR
company_stages.summary: In 2023 Tally made its first hires, starting with customer success. It hired engineers in 2023 and later downscaled that team. By the Tally 2.0 launch in September 2023 it was a team of five. It reached $100K MRR in February 2024; that source gives a team of 3 and over 250,000 users. Tally moved into its first office in 2024.

company_stages.label: Multi-million ARR, still bootstrapped
company_stages.summary: Sources give $2M ARR in February 2025 ($175K MRR) and March 2025 (secondary); both dates are kept. Tally reached $3M ARR in June 2025, $4M ARR in October 2025, $5M ARR in April 2026 and $6M ARR with 2.5 million users in September 2026. It never raised VC and has no external shareholders. Reported team sizes vary across sources: 10, 11, and 4 full-time plus 4 or 5 part-time.

strategy_phases.label: Founder-led outreach and community feedback
strategy_phases.summary: The founders cold-messaged hundreds of makers found on Product Hunt and Twitter. They also joined Slack groups, Reddit and forums to ask for feedback, and invited early users into a Slack channel. They offered instant support and shipped weekly.

strategy_phases.label: Product Hunt launch and building in public
strategy_phases.summary: Tally launched on Product Hunt in March 2021. It shared its journey on Twitter, Indie Hackers and Reddit, which it calls its main marketing channel. It also leaned on no-code communities, newsletters and podcasts.

strategy_phases.label: Free-product-led organic growth
strategy_phases.summary: Growth came from a generous free tier, the 'Made with Tally' badge, word of mouth, SEO and comparison pages, with no paid spend. From early 2023 to early 2025 Tally mostly shipped free features.

strategy_phases.label: Tally 2.0 relaunch
strategy_phases.summary: Tally relaunched as Tally 2.0 on Product Hunt, promoted alongside social media and its newsletter.

strategy_phases.label: Paid experiments and conversion focus
strategy_phases.summary: In 2024 Tally tested YouTube influencer partnerships. In 2025 it ran its first search ads and launched a referral program. It also shifted to shipping highly requested Pro and customization features.

strategy_phases.label: AI search and AI-assistant distribution
strategy_phases.summary: Tally invested in answer-engine and search optimization (AEO/SEO) and tracked citations by large language models (LLMs). It released an MCP server, public API and AI connectors. AI search became its biggest acquisition channel.

strategy_phases.label: Product quality over revenue targets
strategy_phases.summary: For 2026 Tally dropped revenue goals in favor of NPS and user feedback. It rules out enterprise plans, sales calls, partnerships and big launches.

tactics.name: Unlimited free tier as wedge
tactics.description: Give away unlimited forms and responses and nearly all features. Charge only for a single Pro tier.
tactics.mechanism: It removes the paywall frustration users feel with incumbents and differentiates in a crowded market. Wide free usage feeds distribution.

tactics.name: Branded badge on free output
tactics.description: Put a 'Made with Tally' badge on free users' forms. Removing it is a paid feature.
tactics.mechanism: Every form respondent sees the product, so usage turns into acquisition.

tactics.name: Cold DMs to engagers of similar products
tactics.description: Personally message makers who engaged with comparable products on Product Hunt and Twitter/X, asking for feedback.
tactics.mechanism: These are pre-qualified early adopters, and the few who reply become first users and feedback sources.

tactics.name: Try before signup
tactics.description: Let visitors build a form without creating an account until they publish it.
tactics.mechanism: It lowers friction to first value.

tactics.name: Build in public
tactics.description: Share metrics, highs and lows openly on Twitter, Indie Hackers, Reddit and the blog.
tactics.mechanism: It builds audience and trust, and Tally calls it its main marketing channel.

tactics.name: Product Hunt launch and relaunch
tactics.description: Launch on Product Hunt after warming up users, then relaunch a major version later.
tactics.mechanism: It concentrates attention, signups and press into a short window.

tactics.name: Competitor comparison pages and tools
tactics.description: Publish pages comparing the product with the main incumbents, plus an interactive comparison tool built with the product itself.
tactics.mechanism: It captures competitor-keyword search intent while showcasing the product.

tactics.name: Answer-engine optimization (AEO)
tactics.description: Track citations by large language models (LLMs) and keep comparison pages current so AI assistants recommend the product.
tactics.mechanism: AI assistants draw on existing web, forum and user-generated content presence when making recommendations.

tactics.name: Founder-led fast support
tactics.description: Founders personally answer every user question quickly across Slack, email and Twitter.
tactics.mechanism: It builds product love and word of mouth; the founders call it crucial to growth.

tactics.name: Superhuman-style product-market fit survey
tactics.description: Ask users how disappointed they would be without the product.
tactics.mechanism: It quantifies product-market fit and guides product focus.

tactics.name: Embed the product in AI assistants
tactics.description: Ship an MCP server, public API and connectors for ChatGPT, Claude and others.
tactics.mechanism: It lets users create the product's output from inside AI tools.

thirty_second.text: Tally is a bootstrapped form builder from Ghent, Belgium. It gives away unlimited forms and submissions for free, and charges for a single Pro tier, later joined by a Business tier. Free forms carry a 'Made with Tally' badge, so the people who fill out forms see the product. For about five years growth came mainly from that badge, word of mouth and organic search, with little paid spend. Around 2025–2026 AI assistants such as ChatGPT became its largest acquisition channel. Tally reported over $6M ARR and 2.5 million users in September 2026 without raising VC money.

first_users.text: The first users were makers, indie hackers, no-coders and startup founders. A co-founder manually messaged hundreds of people, by one account over 1,000, who had engaged with similar products on Product Hunt and Twitter. The few who replied became the first users and gave feedback. Everyone they talked to was invited into a Slack channel, which grew to about 400 people by late 2020. The founders also answered questions in no-code communities, Reddit and Indie Hackers, offered instant support and shipped features weekly. Tally had about 300 users after its first two to three months and ended 2020 with about 1,500. The March 2021 Product Hunt launch roughly doubled that to 3,000.

flywheel.text: The free plan sets the cycle in motion. Because forms and submissions are unlimited at no cost, many people publish forms. Each free form shows a 'Made with Tally' badge to its respondents, and Tally says most people discover it by filling out a form. Some respondents sign up and create forms of their own. Tally has put the share of free users who upgrade to Pro at about 1–3%, and that revenue funds the company. Word of mouth, personal support, comparison pages and organic search add to this loop. Tally attributes its later AI referrals to years of presence in forums, Reddit and user-generated content, which suggests the earlier organic activity fed the newer channel.

did_differently.text: In a market already held by Google Forms, Typeform and Jotform, Tally competed mainly on price structure rather than features. It gave away unlimited forms, responses and about 99% of features. It paired this with a Notion-style editor where building a form works like typing in a document. It also let people build a form before creating an account. It kept a single Pro tier, built in public, and kept the team small for years. Later, it treated AI assistants as a distribution surface: it shipped an MCP server, a public API and ChatGPT and Claude connectors, and it tracked how often LLMs cited it.

key_takeaways.text: A free tier with no usage limits, combined with a visible badge on the forms people publish, appears to have worked as both the product and the main marketing channel. Tally itself calls the free product its biggest growth engine.

Early traction came from unscalable work: cold DMs to people already engaged with similar products, a Slack group of early users, and founder-run support. The founders say support took around half their time in 2022.

Product Hunt launches produced short spikes rather than steady growth. The 2021 launch doubled users from about 1,500 to 3,000. The 2023 Tally 2.0 relaunch raised weekly signups from about 2,300 to 4,400 for two weeks.

Tally says the growth of its AI referrals rests on years of authentic presence in forums, Reddit and user-generated content. By September 2026, 43% of new users discovered Tally through AI assistants, a channel it says it has never paid for.

Tally spent about two years shipping mostly free features. In 2025 it began rolling out premium customization features, which it says led to an uptick in Pro upgrades. Free-led growth and paid conversion may need separate attention at different stages.

Not every scaling step worked. Tally downscaled an engineering team it hired in 2023 after not getting the desired outcome. It stopped offering discounts because discount users caused more support requests and refunds.
